data.title: New launches to keep Oberoi Realty's sales momentum elevated in FY27
data.description:
Mumbai-based realty major Oberoi Realty outperformed top listed peers in the September quarter on the pre-sales/bookings front. The company reported its highest-ever quarterly pre-sales of ₹9,150 crore in Q2FY27, which was seven times higher year-on-year (Y-o-Y) and nine times higher on a sequential basis. The gains were largely due to the launch of its Gurugram project, Three Sixty North, which received a strong response.
 
After the successful launch of the Gurugram project, the company is eyeing launches of projects/towers across Mumbai and Thane over the next two years. Brokerages are also positive about the steady annuity income from its commercial portfolio, which offers cash flow visibility. At the current price (₹1,802), the stock, which has gained about 14 per cent over the past six months, is trading at a discount to its FY27 net asset value.
 
Of the overall pre-sales in Q2, about 85 per cent was accounted for by Three Sixty North, Gurugram. In the Gurugram project, about 97 per cent of the launched area was booked at a realisation of ₹59,961 per square foot. The rest of the pre-sales were accounted for by its Mumbai projects, Elysian (Goregaon) and 360 West (Worli), at ₹350 crore and ₹280 crore, respectively. Other notable Mumbai project contributions include Sky City and Jardin, which notched up pre-sales of ₹120 crore to ₹180 crore.
 
Elara Securities points out that the realtor delivered a positive surprise on sustenance sales of ₹1,260 crore, which is 25 per cent above both the Street's and its own estimates. This, according to analysts led by Rahul Jain of the brokerage, creates upside risk to the full-year pre-sales estimate of ₹14,400 crore. The company ended the first half of FY27 with pre-sales of ₹10,200 crore. The expectation of higher bookings in FY27 is on account of the planned launches in H2FY27 (Mumbai and adjoining areas), including Peddar Road, one tower each in Pokhran and Kolshet, and uber-luxury villas at Alibaug.
 
The brokerage has a 'buy' rating on the stock with a target price of ₹2,800 and views Oberoi as a low-risk compounder led by prudent underwriting through cycles, with land costs at less than 5 per cent of gross development value. Further, it has a deep micro-market presence with 25 per cent, 14 per cent and 11 per cent volume market shares in Goregaon, Borivali and Mulund, respectively, during FY21-26 and has also evolved into a multi-regional player following the Gurugram launch. It trades at an attractive 20 per cent discount to its March 2027 estimated net asset value.
 
In the annuity business, rental income increased 18 per cent Y-o-Y and 2 per cent sequentially to ₹320 crore during the quarter. The commercial portfolio occupancy stood at 98 per cent during the quarter. The annuity segment's performance was led by Sky City Mall, which achieved 83 per cent occupancy compared to 82 per cent in Q1 and 53 per cent in Q2FY26. Revenues in the hospitality business grew by 2 per cent Y-o-Y to ₹45.6 crore. PL Capital expects annuity income to remain steady at ₹1,300 crore to ₹1,400 crore by FY28, providing strong cash flow visibility. The brokerage has upgraded the stock to 'buy' from 'accumulate', with a target price of ₹2,100.
 
JM Financial Research expects the company to sustain an annual sales run rate of ₹10,000 crore to ₹12,000 crore, compared to ₹4,500 crore to ₹5,500 crore during FY23-26, aided by multiple launches. The annuity vertical, according to analysts led by Sumit Kumar of the brokerage, will also stabilise soon, resulting in strong cash flows that can comfortably support capex and business development. It has a 'buy' rating with a target price of ₹2,250.

data.title: Gamers skip work, crowd gaming cafes for GTA VI as PM Modi joins the buzz
data.description:
Jacob Joel first played Grand Theft Auto in school, then again in college. On Thursday, the 30-year-old IT professional took the day off to play GTA VI in a Bengaluru gaming cafe's mini-theater, steering a speedboat beneath a bridge on a 100-inch projection screen with surround sound.
 
"We waited around 13 long years to get into GTA VI ... that is a nostalgic feeling," Joel said, controller in hand, eyes fixed on the screen.
 
Made for an estimated $1 billion or more, "Grand Theft Auto VI" launched worldwide on Thursday to glowing early reviews, in what is billed as the most anticipated video game release in history.
 
 
In India, one of the world's largest gaming markets with an estimated 550 million players and where most gaming happens on mobile phones, the launch of "Grand Theft Auto VI" turned a console-only title into a social event. It sent players to gaming cafes, drove hours-long live streams and even drew in Prime Minister Narendra Modi, underscoring the growing appeal of premium gaming as a cultural marker.
 
Popular Indian gaming YouTubers CarryMinati and Mythpat each streamed GTA VI for about 10 hours, drawing more than 13 million views apiece by Thursday afternoon.
 
"India is playing a whole new game!" Modi wrote on X, above 10 images modelled on Grand Theft Auto artwork that compared India at the time of GTA V's 2013 release with the country today.
 
Modi has stepped up efforts to woo young voters since youth-led protests over jobs and education pushed his party to sharpen its social media outreach.
 

CAFES FILL CONSOLE GAP

 
Reuters spoke to at least a dozen gamers who crowded gaming cafes in cities including Delhi, Bengaluru and Srinagar on launch day.
 
Because GTA VI is available only on consoles, gaming cafes offered many Indian players a cheaper alternative to buying the hardware. The cafes charge as little as 250 rupees ($2.67) per hour.
 
At the Gaming Mania cafe in Delhi, players sank into tan couches with white controllers, as one complained to another that he had not yet spotted a single bike in the game.
 
Divya Gupta, 48, co-owner of the cafe, said that she had fielded 40 to 50 calls through the day, including from small children asking whether they could play. She said GTA slots were fully pre-booked through Sunday despite a slight price increase.
 
In Bengaluru, Navin Rajendran, 50, owner of the Gamineazy cafe, said the rush was about more than just playing the game.
 
"This is something people want to be seen playing. It's about the bragging rights," he said.

data.title: US Democrats plan 10-yr expiry for deportation orders, green card pathways
data.description:
US House Democrats will introduce legislation on Thursday that would provide relief to certain immigrants facing final orders of removal but with no criminal convictions, while creating a pathway for them to obtain lawful permanent residency, ABC News reported on Wednesday.
 
The proposed legislation, titled the Protect Our Neighbors Act, will be introduced by California Democratic Representative Lateefah Simon, according to the report.
 
Under the proposal, final orders of removal would expire 10 years after they were issued for individuals who have remained continuously in the US and have not been convicted of a crime. Currently, such orders have no expiration date.
  
The proposal has drawn criticism from former New York City Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) field director Scott Mechkowski, who confirmed the development in a post on X.
 
"Your deportation order now comes with an expiration date. That's the Bill House Democrats are introducing tomorrow. They're calling it the Protect Our Neighbors Act," he wrote.
 
Condemning the proposal, Mechkowski said, "Nobody should be rewarded with legal status for ignoring and evading our laws."
 
He outlined how the proposed provision would work.
 
"Here's how it works. A judge orders you removed. You lose your appeals. You don't leave. Stay ten years without a criminal conviction and the order goes away. Then they hand you a path to a green card," he wrote.
 
He argued that the legislation would reward individuals who failed to comply with deportation orders, while those who left the country as directed would not receive similar benefits.
 
"Think about that. The person who obeyed the judge and went home gets nothing. The one who ignored the order gets rewarded," he said.
 
Mechkowski also questioned the provision, arguing that the legislation could undermine the authority of immigration courts.
 
"These people already had their due process. A judge heard the case. It's over. This Bill says a court order means nothing if you outlast it," he wrote.
 
He further argued that delays caused by sanctuary policies could allow individuals to remain in the US long enough for their removal orders to expire. 
ALSO READ: US court strikes down Trump's plan to cap foreign students' visa stays
 
What happens to final deportation orders under the proposed Bill?
 
A final order of removal is issued by an immigration judge or immigration authorities and requires a non-US citizen to leave the country. The order becomes final after administrative appeals have been exhausted or the deadline for filing an appeal has passed.
 
Although a final removal order gives ICE the legal authority to deport an individual, it does not mean deportation takes place immediately or automatically. Removal proceedings can be delayed or suspended because of deferred action, a stay of removal, ongoing litigation or other circumstances.
 
Under the proposed legislation, an immigration judge could renew an expired final order of removal if the government establishes, through "clear and convincing evidence", that there was a substantial reason for the delay in carrying out the order.
 
The reason would have to be unrelated to administrative or funding delays. The judge would also have to determine that renewing the order was in the public interest based on new evidence, according to ABC report.
 
While Mechkowski criticised the legislation, immigration expert Andrea Flores welcomed the proposal.
 
"Glad to see the Protect Our Neighbors Act, which would create an earned path to legal residency for immigrants who may be left out of the American Dream and Promise Act," she wrote on X.
 
The legislation is also co-sponsored by California Democratic Representatives John Garamendi, Zoe Lofgren and Juan Vargas.
 
Former acting ICE Director Todd Lyons told lawmakers in February that approximately 1.6 million people in the US had final orders of deportation.
 
US deportations of Indian nationals
 
The proposed legislation comes amid expanded immigration enforcement under US President Donald Trump's second administration. The Department of Homeland Security and ICE have stepped up action against individuals with final orders of removal, including deportations to third countries.
 
Even immigrants who have regularly attended mandatory immigration check-ins have faced renewed risks of detention and deportation.
 
The development also follows Trump's remarks to CBS News' 60 Minutes, in which he said he would "love to do something on immigration" with Democrats, who are set to take control of both chambers of Congress in January following their victories in the midterm elections.
 
According to India's Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), the US deported 4,840 Indian nationals between January 2025 and July 2026. More than 6,000 Indians were deported during Trump's first presidential term, between 2017 and 2021.

data.title: Yes Bank AT-1 bondholders urge RBI to prioritise investor protection
data.description:
Holders of  Yes Bank's AT-1 bonds have written to the country's central bank, urging it to prioritise investor protection after it sought a review of a Supreme Court ruling that restored these bonds last month, according to a copy of the letter reviewed by Reuters.
 
The dispute stems from Yes Bank's rescue in 2020, when authorities wrote off ₹84.15 billion worth of additional Tier-1 (AT-1) bonds, a type of security designed to absorb losses when banks run into trouble.
 
Last month, the Supreme Court ruled the write-off illegal over procedural lapses and ordered the bonds restored. However, review petitions by the bank and the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) have delayed relief for investors.
 
 
Bondholders, in their letter dated November 18, said the RBI had remained "absent" in its capacity as the regulator "responsible for protecting the interests of the investing public and the integrity of the banking system".
 
Acting on behalf of the bondholders, Axis Trustee Services Limited has separately filed a contempt petition in the Supreme Court, alleging that Yes Bank and its directors have failed to comply with court directions and have not taken any steps to restore the bonds.
 
In the contempt petition, a copy of which has been reviewed by Reuters, the trustee said bondholders, including retail investors, pension funds and provident funds, had been deprived of their investments for more than six years and still had no visibility on the restoration of the bonds and payment of coupons.
 
The trustee argued that the bank could not avoid complying with the ruling while pursuing other legal remedies because the judgment remained in force.
 
The bondholders, in their letter to the central bank, said they expected the RBI to oversee implementation of the Supreme Court verdict and protect investors rather than align itself with further challenges to the ruling.
 
The RBI and Yes Bank did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

data.title: Six listed REITs distribute ₹3,234 crore in Q2 FY27 to 5.25 lakh investors
data.description:
India's six publicly listed Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) distributed a combined ₹3,234 crore to more than 5.25 lakh unitholders in the second quarter of FY27, according to data released by the Indian REITs Association. The distribution was nearly 39% higher than the ₹2,331 crore paid out in Q2 FY26, when five REITs were listed. In Q2 FY25, the four listed REITs distributed ₹1,383 crore.
 
The six listed trusts are Brookfield India Real Estate Trust, Embassy Office Parks REIT, Mindspace Business Parks REIT, Nexus Select Trust, Knowledge Realty Trust and Bagmane Prime Office REIT.
 
The sector's gross assets under management (AUM) stood at more than ₹3.30 lakh crore as of Q2 FY27. Its combined market capitalisation exceeded ₹2.09 lakh crore as of November 17, 2026.
 
 
Together, the six REITs manage more than 215 million sq ft of Grade A office and retail space across India. Since their inception, they have distributed more than ₹38,000 crore to unitholders.
 
The rise in quarterly distributions comes alongside an increase in the number of listed REITs. Knowledge Realty Trust and Bagmane Prime Office REIT have joined the four earlier listed trusts, expanding the range of listed property assets available to investors.
 
“The distribution of ₹3,234 crore during the quarter reflects the strength of India's REIT sector and its underlying assets,” said Shirish Godbole, chief executive officer of Knowledge Realty Trust and chairperson of the Indian REITs Association.
 
He said demand for office space from Global Capability Centres (GCCs) and front-office enterprises was supporting the sector. Healthy occupancy levels and rental collections, he added, were helping sustain distributions to investors.
 
REITs allow investors to gain exposure to income-generating commercial real estate without having to buy and manage an entire property. Investors purchase units listed on stock exchanges, while the trust owns and manages a portfolio of properties and distributes income to unitholders.
 
The quarterly distribution figure is an aggregate payout across the six trusts. It should not be confused with the return earned by an individual investor. The actual income received depends on the number of units held and the distribution declared by the particular REIT.
 
Investors should also distinguish between distributions and total returns. A REIT's total return includes both the income distributed and any change in the market price of its units. Unit prices can rise or fall with interest rates, property valuations, occupancy, rental growth and broader market conditions.
 
The distribution figure alone does not establish whether payouts have increased on a like-for-like basis across the trusts. The sector's expansion from four listed REITs in Q2 FY25 to six in Q2 FY27 also contributes to the increase in the aggregate amount distributed.
 
For investors evaluating REITs, factors such as occupancy, tenant concentration, lease expiries, debt levels, borrowing costs, rental escalations and the quality of the underlying properties remain important. Distributions are not fixed or guaranteed.
 
The Indian REITs Association, a non-profit industry body formed in 2023 under the guidance of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), represents the six listed trusts.

data.title: Trump, Xi and Putin hold first ever trilateral talks amid global tensions
data.description:
President Donald Trump met for more than an hour on Thursday with China's Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin, a moment that could mark a pivot in world history - or become a quickly forgotten photo op.

Trump has promoted this first-ever three-way meeting with Xi and Putin - two of America's leading rivals - as a chance to hash out rules for controlling nuclear arms and to start resolving the wars in Ukraine and Iran. Experts have kept expectations low for major breakthroughs.

"We are really making history," Trump said. "The United States, Russia and China are uniquely positioned to discuss how to reduce the number of nuclear weapons on Earth and also to lessen the risk of those weapons being used." "We will be having discussions on the theme of promoting world peace," Xi said at the start of the trilateral meeting. State broadcaster CCTV said Xi told his counterparts that he thinks nuclear weapons should be prohibited and destroyed, and called for the building of a nuclear-weapon-free world.

 

Putin harkened back to Russia, China and America's shared history as "victors in World War II," saying that "we hold joint responsibility for maintaining international peace." The last nuclear arms pact between Russia and the United States, known as New START, expired in February, and Trump has said he wants "a new, improved and modernized" deal that includes China. But China has less motivation to accept limits given that its arsenal of more than 600 warheads is far smaller than the more than 5,000 warheads believed to be in each of the US and Russian stockpiles.

"Once you have the nuclear weapons, it's very hard not to have them," Trump said. "So it's not an easy thing to do, give them up." Daryl Kimball, executive director of the Arms Control Association, said Trump's showmanship could at best start a process that would eventually lead to a sustained set of talks for reducing nuclear arsenals.

"We need more than diplomatic theater and photo opportunities between Xi, Putin and Trump at APEC," Kimball said. "And one meeting will not likely produce dramatic breakthroughs."

The leaders also talked about Iran and trade

Before the three-way meeting began on Thursday afternoon, the US president had a separate one-on-one meeting with Xi - their third substantial meeting this year. The US president praised their friendship and their shared interest in having oil shipped through the Strait of Hormuz, which has become a key site of attacks in the Iran war. Trump suggested he would push Xi to buy more agricultural products from America.

Xi said that relations between the US and China have been "generally stable and improved" during Trump's presidency. The official Chinese news agency Xinhua reported that Xi discussed Taiwan with Trump and said the two countries needed to improve communication on economic and trade issues.

Trump also added a separate sit-down with Putin to his Thursday schedule, marking the first time the leaders have held talks since their discussions in Alaska last year that failed to broker a deal to ease Russia's war in Ukraine.

"Wonderful things can come out of this - or at least start," Trump said after joining Putin for the one-on-one meeting on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Summit, calling Putin "my friend." "We've had a great relationship for many years," Trump said after shaking hands with Putin. Their meeting lasted roughly 40 minutes.

Trump has frequently boasted of his rapport with Putin, even as relations between the US and Ukraine appear to have cratered recently. Trump rejected new Russia sanctions, while Kyiv was undermined by disruptions in satellite support for its drones during the war.

The US president added another agenda item to the trilateral meeting. He said at its opening that the trio would talk about ways to "protect our nation's sovereignty from rogue globalist organizations such as the International Criminal Court."

Trump boasts about his relationships. But the ties between Xi and Putin are stronger

The US president's ambitions recall an era of great power politics when wealthier countries felt entitled to decide the fate of seemingly lesser nations. Trump is negotiating with China and Russia without the involvement of Ukraine - or countries like Germany, France, the United Kingdom, Japan and South Korea that also have stakes in the outcome of any talks.

The US president has openly pursued a Nobel Peace Prize while also taking military actions against Venezuela and Iran.

Trump has long believed his ability to create personal connections gives him a diplomatic edge. Xi appealed to his ego Wednesday by greeting Air Force One on the airport tarmac, as the two leaders turned their handshake into a one-armed hug.

But Trump does not appear to always have the same deep relationship based on common interests that Xi and Putin share. For all the compliments the US president has showered on the two autocrats, the warmth has not always been mutually effusive.

On Wednesday at APEC, Xi greeted Putin by calling him "my old friend." The Russian leader responded by declaring Xi to be his "dear friend." China has helped economically support Russia after its 2022 invasion of Ukraine, providing Putin with a financial lifeline after the US and its allies imposed new sanctions.

By contrast, when Xi came to the White House for a state visit in September, he was far more restrained with Trump, saying they had built a "personal rapport and stayed in touch." Trump and Xi plan to meet a total of four times this year, with their final time together coming in December at the G20 summit being held at the Trump National Doral Golf Club in Florida.

Still, there were signs of friction Thursday in the US-China relationship despite Trump's praise of Xi.

Chinese officials blocked a Bloomberg reporter, Annmarie Hordern, from the trilateral meeting after she asked a question at the earlier Trump-Xi session.

Chinese television showed a video of Trump appearing drowsy, while the White House posted a clip of Trump helping Xi up an escalator.

Conflicts on AI also hang over the meetings

While Trump views his relationship with China as a positive, it has not necessarily resulted in meaningful changes between the world's two largest economies. China continues to run large trade surpluses with the rest of the world, while the US has almost equally large trade deficits.

And the race between the US and China to master artificial intelligence has grown tense over the past two weeks. Trump's ally Jensen Huang resigned last week as the CEO of Nvidia after confessing to an extramarital affair with a woman, Alice Huang, whose company helped to give China access to the company's advanced computer chips used to develop AI models. Beijing has denied that Alice Huang was a Chinese government agent.

Trump held off on imposing tougher restrictions on China's ability to access the chips, suggesting he did not want to insult China and aggravate relations.

US officials have said that China had not fully honoured its commitments made last year in a Trump-Xi meeting to buy more US agricultural products and loosen restrictions on the sale of rare earth minerals needed for electronics.

The trade truce between the US and China reached last year after duelling tariff hikes is set to expire by Jan. 10 next year.

Meanwhile, both China and Russia have used trade to support Iran, even during the US war on that country, which has pushed up energy prices and reduced global economic growth.

data.title: Canada approves 2.52 lakh visitor visas for Indians in 2026, up 20.8%
data.description:
Canada approved 816,745 visitor visas between January and August 2026, an increase of 10.6 per cent from the 738,565 visas issued during the corresponding period last year, according to newly released data from Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC).
 
India accounted for the largest share of approvals, with 252,145 visitor visas issued to Indian citizens during the eight-month period. This was 20.8 per cent higher than the 208,675 visas approved in the same period in 2025.
 
The increase comes after a sharp decline in Canadian visitor visa approvals last year. While the latest figures point to a recovery, the total remains well below the level recorded in 2024.
  
The country-level data also reveal contrasting trends. Approvals for Pakistani nationals rose 24.5 per cent, while those for Nigerians fell 23.7 per cent. The Philippines, meanwhile, recorded only a marginal increase.
 
Canada visitor visa approval and refusal rates
 
2024: National temporary resident visa (TRV) refusal rate – 54 per cent
2025: National TRV refusal rate – 51 per cent
January-February 2025: Visitor visa approval rate, excluding super visas – 46 per cent
January-February 2026: Visitor visa approval rate, excluding super visas – 52 per cent
 
However, these national approval and refusal rates do not establish the likelihood of an individual applicant from a particular country receiving a visa.
 
The country-level figures released by IRCC show the number of visas approved for each nationality, rather than the proportion of applications approved.
 
Canada visitor visa approvals: 2024 to 2026
 
Canada's visitor visa approvals have fluctuated considerably over the past three years.
 
IRCC approved 1,080,420 visitor visas between January and August 2024. The figure dropped to 738,565 during the same period in 2025, a decline of 31.6 per cent.
 
Approvals recovered by 10.6 per cent in the first eight months of 2026, but remained below the 2024 level.
 
Canada visitor visa approvals: 2024 to 2026
 
January-August 2024: 1,080,420 visas approved
January-August 2025: 738,565 visas approved, down 31.6 per cent year-on-year
January-August 2026: 816,745 visas approved, up 10.6 per cent year-on-year
 
Top 10 countries receiving the most Canadian visitor visas in 2026
 
India continued to lead the country-wise rankings by a considerable margin, with 252,145 visitor visas approved between January and August 2026.
 
China ranked second, with 141,900 approvals. Together, Indian and Chinese nationals accounted for nearly 48 per cent of all visitor visas issued during the period.
 
Colombia ranked third, followed by Ukraine and Nigeria.
 
Top 10 countries receiving the most Canadian visitor visas in 2026
 
1. India: 252,145 approvals (+20.8 per cent)
2. China: 141,900 (-0.3 per cent)
3. Colombia: 35,605 (+27.6 per cent)
4. Ukraine: 27,040 (+82.2 per cent)
5. Nigeria: 26,210 (-23.7 per cent)
6. Mexico: 24,590 (-2.8 per cent)
7. Pakistan: 19,315 (+24.5 per cent)
8. Jamaica: 18,285 (-3.6 per cent)
9. Algeria: 16,165 (+38.9 per cent)
10. Philippines: 15,555 (+2.1 per cent)
 
India, Pakistan, Nigeria and the Philippines: How approvals changed
 
The four countries recorded different trends in Canadian visitor visa approvals between 2024 and 2026.
 
While approvals declined for all four in 2025 compared with 2024, India and Pakistan registered strong recoveries this year. Nigeria continued to see a decline, while the Philippines recorded little change.
 
India: 380,630 in 2024; 208,675 in 2025; 252,145 in 2026 (+20.8 per cent).
Pakistan: 22,450 in 2024; 15,510 in 2025; 19,315 in 2026 (+24.5 per cent).
Nigeria: 35,185 in 2024; 34,360 in 2025; 26,210 in 2026 (-23.7 per cent).
Philippines: 40,365 in 2024; 15,235 in 2025; 15,555 in 2026 (+2.1 per cent).
 
Pakistan recorded the largest percentage increase among the four countries. India, however, contributed the biggest absolute increase in approvals.
 
Nigeria's numbers moved in the opposite direction, while the Philippines remained considerably below its 2024 level.
 
India accounts for more than half of Canada's visitor visa recovery
 
India's position as Canada's largest source of visitor visa approvals became even more pronounced in 2026.
 
Between January and August, IRCC approved 252,145 visitor visas for Indian citizens, compared with 208,675 during the corresponding period in 2025. This represents an increase of 43,470 approvals, or 20.8 per cent.
 
The increase is particularly notable when compared with Canada's overall recovery. The country issued 78,180 more visitor visas during the first eight months of 2026 than in the same period last year. India's additional 43,470 approvals accounted for more than 55 per cent of that increase.
 
Indian nationals also accounted for approximately 31 per cent of all Canadian visitor visas approved during the period.
 
For Indians planning to visit family members, relatives or friends in Canada, the rise in approvals provides an indication of the increased volume of visas being issued. However, it does not necessarily mean that individual applicants have a higher probability of success.
 
IRCC's processing-times update on October 7, 2026, estimated a 30-day processing time for visitor visa applications from India.
 
Pakistan records the highest percentage increase
 
Pakistan recorded a 24.5 per cent increase in Canadian visitor visa approvals during January-August 2026, the highest growth rate among the four countries compared.
 
IRCC approved 19,315 visitor visas for Pakistani nationals during the period, up from 15,510 in the corresponding eight months of 2025.
 
The increase follows a decline from 22,450 approvals in January-August 2024 to 15,510 in 2025.
 
Despite the recovery, the latest figure remains below the 2024 level.
 
Do higher visitor visa approvals mean better chances of getting a visa?
 
Not necessarily. An increase in the number of visitor visas issued does not automatically mean that applicants have a higher approval rate. According to IRCC, the number of approvals can rise because more people have applied, because IRCC has processed a larger number of applications, or because a higher proportion of applications have been approved.

data.title: India health supplements market to nearly double to $9.4 bn by FY31
data.description:
India's health supplements market is expected to nearly double from about USD 5.3 billion in FY26 to USD 9.4 billion by FY31, Redseer Strategy Consultants said in a report on Thursday.
 The report, 'Health Supplements in India: From Medicine Cabinet to Daily Nutrition', said the market is shifting from reactive, medicinal use to daily preventive wellness, driven by post-COVID health awareness, social media content, format innovation, such as gummies and effervescents, and rising digital commerce.
 Protein and sports nutrition, growing around 19 per cent CAGR, and specialty bio-actives at about 16 per cent CAGR are emerging as the fastest-growing segments, the strategy consultancy firm said.
 
 Redseer noted significant headroom for expansion, pointing to India's projected 2030 per capita supplement spend gap compared with Indonesia (1.2x), China (2x) and the US (22x).
 India's health supplements market is on course to reach approximately USD 9.4 billion by FY31, the report said.
Quick commerce is expected to command 40-50 per cent of online supplement spending, compared with approximately 19 per cent currently.
 Digital native brands (DNBs) are expected to drive over one-third of the market by FY31.
 Looking ahead, the report said future growth will hinge on product differentiation in established categories like protein and multivitamins (USD 3.5-4 billion by FY31), awareness-led scaling in proven categories such as creatine and omega-3 (USD 2.8-3.3 billion), and clinically backed solutions for weight management, gut and women's health (USD 1.3-1.8 billion).
 Expanding into adjacent functional food and beverage and beauty and personal care categories could widen the addressable market to USD 100-125 billion by FY31, it added.
 Kushal Bhatnagar, Partner, Redseer Strategy Consultants, said, "The economics of supplements are quite different from those of most consumer categories. A brand can acquire a customer on the strength of a compelling health proposition, but the real test comes several weeks later, when the consumer decides whether the product has earned a place in their daily routine."
